ARI.brief: Jacoby Brissett opens camp as the starter with rookie Carson Beck behind him, and the staff has been openly complimentary of Beck after his Hall of Fame Game showing, so this is a live competition rather than a settled room. The offense runs through Trey McBride, who has been a target hog regardless of who plays quarterback. Rookie Jeremiyah Love, the No. 3 overall pick, arrives as a three-down back and pushes James Conner (foot) into a complementary role.

ATL.brief: Tua Tagovailoa is the starter but is carrying a back issue, and Michael Penix Jr. is working back from ACL surgery, so the quarterback picture is less settled than the depth chart suggests. Bijan Robinson is the offense's engine and among the highest-volume backs in football. Drake London and Kyle Pitts are the passing-game priorities, and both benefit if Tagovailoa's timing-based game holds up.

BAL.brief: Lamar Jackson is not playing in the preseason opener but is otherwise healthy and working closely with rookie receiver Lane. Derrick Henry is still the early-down and goal-line back at 32. Zay Flowers (quadriceps) is the No. 1 receiver when right; cornerback Nate Wiggins was carted off with a lower-body injury, which matters more for the defense than the fantasy offense.

BUF.brief: Josh Allen is the safest asset in fantasy football and now has DJ Moore as a genuine outside threat alongside Khalil Shakir and Keon Coleman. James Cook remains the lead back with Ray Davis and Ty Johnson (knee) behind him. Guard Connor McGovern is banged up, which is worth tracking for a line that has been a strength.

CAR.brief: Bryce Young enters his fourth season with Tetairoa McMillan established as a legitimate No. 1 receiver after Offensive Rookie of the Year honors. The backfield is genuinely muddled: Chuba Hubbard and Jonathon Brooks are ranked within a few spots of each other and neither has separated. The offensive line is a concern with Taylor Moton and Ikem Ekwonu both opening on PUP.

CHI.brief: Caleb Williams is in his third season and the expert market has cooled on him relative to a year ago. Colston Loveland has emerged as a top-three fantasy tight end in consensus, which is a real signal about target priority. Luther Burden III is sidelined with a groin injury and Rome Odunze is the other primary receiver; D'Andre Swift leads a backfield that rookie Kyle Monangai is pushing.

CIN.brief: One of the cleanest offensive situations in the league: Joe Burrow is healthy and set to play in the preseason opener, and there are no notable injuries on the skill-position depth chart. Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are both locked in, and the passing volume behind them is thin, which concentrates targets. Chase Brown is the unquestioned lead back and a top-10 PPR option because of his receiving role.

CLE.brief: Shedeur Sanders is listed ahead of Deshaun Watson, though Watson is reportedly being carried as a co-starter on the depth chart, so the room is not fully resolved. Harold Fannin Jr. has climbed into the top five at tight end in consensus, an unusually strong signal for a young player. Quinshon Judkins leads the backfield with Dylan Sampson behind him; the receiver group is young and unsettled.

DAL.brief: Dak Prescott is healthy and the supporting cast is loaded with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, though Pickens is on a franchise tag and his long-term future is already a talking point. Javonte Williams is the lead back after re-signing, with Jaydon Blue behind him. The line has multiple minor injuries (Tyler Guyton, Ajani Cornelius) but no season-altering absence.

DEN.brief: Bo Nix is the starter and the receiver room changed shape with Jaylen Waddle joining Courtland Sutton. Waddle, Marvin Mims and Michael Woods are all carrying minor injuries, so early-camp usage reports are noisy. The backfield is a three-way problem between J.K. Dobbins, RJ Harvey and Jonah Coleman, and no source has it settled. Denver's defense is the consensus No. 1 fantasy unit.

DET.brief: Jared Goff returns with Amon-Ra St. Brown and Sam LaPorta, and Goff has publicly said the team needs to find more ways to get LaPorta the ball. Jahmyr Gibbs is the RB1 in fantasy and just signed a record running back contract; he is listed questionable with a back issue but has no meaningful competition after David Montgomery's departure. Isiah Pacheco (knee) is the primary backup.

GB.brief: Jordan Love will start the preseason opener against Pittsburgh and the coaching staff has been effusive about his arm talent. Josh Jacobs (groin) is the lead back. The tight end room is decimated -- Tucker Kraft is working back from an ACL injury while Luke Musgrave, Luke Lachey and RJ Maryland are all sidelined -- which raises the risk on Kraft's strong ranking. The receiver group is a committee.

HOU.brief: C.J. Stroud enters a season where Houston's postseason ceiling is a live question, and Nico Collins is the clear No. 1 receiver. Tank Dell is still working back from a major knee injury, which opens snaps for second-year receivers Jayden Higgins and Jaylin Noel. David Montgomery leads the backfield with rookie-contract back Woody Marks in a change-of-pace role.

IND.brief: The quarterback situation is the story: Daniel Jones is listed first but Anthony Richardson is starting Thursday against New England and Jones is not playing in the preseason, which makes the Week 1 starter genuinely uncertain. Jonathan Taylor is the offense regardless and one of the highest-volume backs in football. Tyler Warren is a top-five fantasy tight end; Alec Pierce (ankle, PUP) and Josh Downs (groin) are both limited.

JAX.brief: Trevor Lawrence has a deep, young receiver group -- Brian Thomas Jr., Parker Washington, Jakobi Meyers and Travis Hunter -- which is the main reason no single Jacksonville receiver is priced as a true alpha. Head coach Liam Coen has confirmed starters will sit against New Orleans. The backfield belongs to Bhayshul Tuten with Chris Rodriguez and LeQuint Allen behind him. Injuries are limited to the interior line.

KC.brief: Patrick Mahomes is listed questionable with a knee (ACL) designation, which is the single most important thing to track on this roster. The skill group was rebuilt around Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy (shoulder) and Kenneth Walker III, with Travis Kelce still a fixture. Justin Fields is the backup quarterback, which changes the offense's shape considerably if Mahomes misses time.

LAC.brief: Justin Herbert is described as getting comfortable in a new offense, which is the key context for every Chargers pass catcher. Omarion Hampton is a clear lead back entering Year 2 after an injury-shortened rookie season. Ladd McConkey is the primary target; rookie tight end Oronde Gadsden II has already climbed into TE2 territory in consensus. Left tackle Rashawn Slater is banged up.

LAR.brief: Matthew Stafford is back with Puka Nacua as a target monopolist and Davante Adams as the complementary veteran. Kyren Williams remains the lead back with Blake Corum behind him, a split that has frustrated fantasy managers for three seasons. The tight end room is a committee between rookie Terrance Ferguson and Colby Parkinson. The Rams defense is a consensus top-four fantasy unit.

LV.brief: Rookie Fernando Mendoza is listed as the starter over Kirk Cousins, who was held out of practice after an altercation involving Maxx Crosby -- an unsettled situation worth monitoring. Brock Bowers is the centerpiece of the passing game and Michael Mayer is a usable second tight end. Ashton Jeanty is the workhorse back in Year 2. The receiver room is thin and injury-hit.

MIA.brief: Malik Willis is the starter with rookie Quinn Ewers behind him, a significant downgrade in passing quality that suppresses every Miami receiver. That makes De'Von Achane the entire offense: head coach Jeff Hafley has said Achane could see 40-plus touches in some games. The receiver group led by Malik Washington is one of the least valuable in the league.

MIN.brief: Kyler Murray has been named the starting quarterback over J.J. McCarthy, the most consequential camp decision of the week for fantasy. Justin Jefferson remains an elite target earner and Murray's mobility changes the offense's structure. The backfield is a committee between Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason with neither separating. Jordan Addison is dealing with a thumb injury.

NE.brief: Drake Maye is sitting out the preseason opener but is entrenched as the starter and now throws to A.J. Brown, acquired in June. TreVeyon Henderson and Rhamondre Stevenson split the backfield and Henderson's market value has fallen sharply, suggesting drafters no longer expect a clean takeover. Hunter Henry remains the tight end. The receiver room behind Brown is thin.

NO.brief: Tyler Shough is entering his second season as the starter and is a common pick for a Year 2 leap. Chris Olave is coming off a career year and is the clear No. 1, with rookie Jordyn Tyson behind him. Travis Etienne Jr. arrived to lead the backfield and Alvin Kamara is now a complementary piece; Etienne's market value has fallen hard, so drafters are skeptical of the split.

NYG.brief: Jaxson Dart is a popular Year 2 breakout pick and the offense added Isaiah Likely at tight end. The critical variable is Malik Nabers, who is listed questionable while working back from a torn ACL. Cam Skattebo is the lead back after an impressive but injury-shortened rookie season, with Tyrone Tracy Jr. behind him. The receiver room behind Nabers is thin and banged up.

NYJ.brief: Geno Smith is the starter and Garrett Wilson is the clear No. 1 receiver coming off an injury-shortened season. Breece Hall returns on the franchise tag as the lead back with Braelon Allen behind him. The tight end room now features rookie Kenyon Sadiq (abdomen) alongside Mason Taylor. Cornerback Qwan'tez Stiggers was taken to a hospital after collapsing at practice.

PHI.brief: Jalen Hurts anchors an offense that still runs through Saquon Barkley, who is looking to rebound from a down 2025. DeVonta Smith (hamstring) is the top receiver and his market value is rising sharply. Right tackle Lane Johnson has said 2026 is likely his final season, and the backfield behind Barkley is thin with Elijah Mitchell on IR and Dameon Pierce hurt.

PIT.brief: Aaron Rodgers is listed as the starter with rookie Drew Allar third on the depth chart. The receiver room pairs DK Metcalf (unspecified injury) with Michael Pittman Jr. (leg), and both are currently limited. The backfield is a true committee between Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle, ranked one spot apart in consensus, with rookie Kaleb Johnson behind them. A first-round pick is likely to miss the preseason opener.

SEA.brief: Sam Darnold is the starter and Jaxon Smith-Njigba is the reigning Offensive Player of the Year and a consensus top-three fantasy receiver. The backfield is unsettled: Zach Charbonnet opened on PUP with a knee (ACL) issue and rookie Jadarian Price is banged up, so the lead role is unresolved. Cooper Kupp and Rashid Shaheed are complementary pieces. Seattle's defense is a top-three fantasy unit.

SF.brief: Christian McCaffrey has now missed multiple consecutive practices, and at 30 that is the single most important thing on this roster to track -- his market value has still been rising. Brock Purdy throws to a rebuilt group led by Mike Evans (quadriceps) and Deebo Samuel, with Ricky Pearsall on IR after PCL surgery. George Kittle remains a top-10 tight end. Jordan James is the handcuff.

TB.brief: Baker Mayfield returns with Emeka Egbuka as the leading receiver after a rookie season that started hot and faded. Chris Godwin is back and sources disagree sharply on him. Bucky Irving is the lead back after a disappointing, injury-shortened 2025, with Kenny Gainwell in a complementary role. Left tackle Tristan Wirfs (hamstring) and Jalen McMillan (calf) are both limited.

TEN.brief: Cam Ward enters his second season with a reshaped receiver room built around rookie Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson, with Calvin Ridley now the third option. Tony Pollard leads a backfield that Tyjae Spears splits into, and neither is a workhorse. Gunnar Helm is the tight end. This is one of the lower-volume passing offenses in the league by consensus expectation.

WAS.brief: Jayden Daniels is the offense and his rushing floor makes him a top-five fantasy quarterback. Left tackle Laremy Tunsil has a torn triceps and will reportedly miss most of the season, a meaningful hit to Daniels' protection. Terry McLaurin is the No. 1 receiver with Stefon Diggs' market value rising. The backfield is split between Rachaad White and Jacory Croskey-Merritt, who has been one of the biggest risers in August rankings.

9509.outlook: Top-five among backs in carries, rushing yards, touches and fantasy points in each of the past two seasons, and he is the entire Atlanta offense on the ground. No injury designation and no committee threat behind him; Brian Robinson Jr. is a short-yardage complement, not a rival. His receiving role is what separates him in full PPR. Sources are unanimous inside RB1-2, and market value is rising.
9509.watch: Tua Tagovailoa's back issue -- a downgrade at quarterback would stack more boxes against him.

9221.outlook: Top-10 among backs in yards per carry, routes, targets, receptions and touchdowns in all three of his seasons, with 38 touchdowns over the past two. David Montgomery is gone, so the touch ceiling that capped him (never higher than seventh in touches) should finally lift. He just signed a record running back contract, which confirms Detroit's intent to feed him. Listed questionable with a back issue in early August.
9221.watch: The back designation -- any lingering issue would be the only thing standing between him and a career-high workload.

7564.outlook: Has finished four of his five seasons no lower than fifth in receiver fantasy points per game. Cincinnati's depth chart is unusually clean this camp with no notable skill-position injuries, and target competition behind him and Tee Higgins is thin. Joe Burrow is healthy and playing in the preseason opener. Consensus WR1 with essentially no dissent among the five sources.
7564.watch: Burrow's availability -- Chase's ceiling is entirely tied to it.

9493.outlook: Has been one of the most heavily targeted receivers in football in each of his three seasons and remains the clear No. 1 in Los Angeles even with Davante Adams alongside him. Matthew Stafford's presence keeps the volume stable. Healthy with no designation. Market value has softened over the past 30 days despite unchanged expert ranks, which is the only bearish signal on him.
9493.watch: Stafford's health -- the Rams' backup quarterback situation would materially cut Nacua's ceiling.

9488.outlook: The reigning Offensive Player of the Year led all receivers in target share (36%), receiving yards and air yards. All five sources have him exactly WR3, the tightest agreement of any player on the board. Sam Darnold returns at quarterback, so there is continuity. Healthy with no designation. Market value has drifted down slightly, likely age-and-price mechanics rather than anything about his role.
9488.watch: Whether a 36% target share is repeatable if Seattle adds a second real threat.

7547.outlook: The only player in NFL history with 90-plus catches in each of his first five seasons, and Detroit's offensive structure has not changed. All five sources have him exactly WR4. Jared Goff is back and Jameson Williams remains the field-stretcher rather than a target rival. Healthy, and market value is trending up.
7547.watch: Sam LaPorta's target share -- Goff has said publicly the team wants to feed the tight end more.

4034.outlook: Led all running backs in snaps, routes, touches, targets, receptions and receiving yards in a bounce-back 2025, and he remains the highest-leverage PPR back when healthy. The problem is now: he has missed multiple consecutive practices in August and is listed questionable at age 30. Market value has risen sharply anyway, which suggests drafters are treating the absence as maintenance. Jordan James is the direct handcuff.
4034.watch: Whether he returns to full practice before the season -- his profile has no margin for a soft-tissue issue at 30.

6813.outlook: Has improved his fantasy points per game in each of the past three seasons and delivered his best production since 2021 last year. He is the offense in Indianapolis regardless of who starts at quarterback, which matters because the Daniel Jones and Anthony Richardson competition is genuinely open. No injury designation. His market value has fallen over the past month, the largest drop among top-five backs.
6813.watch: The quarterback decision -- a Richardson start changes Indianapolis's game scripts and red-zone distribution.

6794.outlook: Still an elite target earner, but the context changed: Kyler Murray has been named the starter over J.J. McCarthy, which brings more scrambling and a less predictable dropback structure. Sources are tightly grouped at WR5-8. His market value has fallen more than any receiver in the top 10 over the past 30 days, which reads as the market pricing quarterback uncertainty. Jordan Addison (thumb) is the secondary option.
6794.watch: How Murray's off-schedule play affects Jefferson's target rate -- the first two preseason games should tell.

12527.outlook: Workhorse back entering Year 2 after an uneven rookie season that still produced heavy volume (seventh among backs in carries and targets). Las Vegas has no meaningful competition behind him. The complication is the offense around him: rookie Fernando Mendoza is listed ahead of Kirk Cousins, and a rookie quarterback usually means fewer scoring opportunities. FantasyPros has him a full three spots higher than the other four sources.
12527.watch: The quarterback resolution -- Jeanty's touchdown equity depends on whether Las Vegas can move the ball.

8138.outlook: Remains Buffalo's lead back in the league's most efficient scoring offense, which is the single best touchdown environment available to a running back. Ray Davis and Ty Johnson (knee) are complementary. Sources spread him from RB5 to RB9, a reasonable gap that reflects genuine disagreement over how much of the goal-line work Josh Allen takes. Market value is flat.
8138.watch: Goal-line usage -- Allen's rushing touchdowns are the direct tax on Cook's ceiling.

6786.outlook: Coming off his worst fantasy finish since 2021 (12th among receivers in points per game) despite clearing 1,000 yards. Dak Prescott is healthy and the offense should be more stable, but George Pickens is now a legitimate second alpha, which caps Lamb's target share relative to his 2023 peak. Sources agree tightly at WR5-7. Market value is slightly up.
6786.watch: Whether Pickens' presence lowers Lamb's target share or simply raises the offense's total volume.

9226.outlook: Scored 11 or 12 touchdowns in each of his three seasons and is now, functionally, the entire Miami offense. Head coach Jeff Hafley has said publicly that Achane could see 40-plus touches in some games. The offsetting factor is severe: Malik Willis is the starting quarterback with rookie Quinn Ewers behind him, so scoring chances will be scarce. ESPN is highest on him at RB5, FantasyPros lowest at RB8.
9226.watch: Whether the promised volume actually materialises -- at his size, 40 touches is a durability question as much as an opportunity one.

12507.outlook: Primed for a breakout after an injury-shortened rookie year in which he averaged 13.8 carries and 3.9 targets across nine appearances. He is the unquestioned lead back and the receiving work is what makes him a PPR asset. Justin Herbert is described as still getting comfortable in a new offense, which is a modest early-season risk. Market value is rising sharply.
12507.watch: Whether the new scheme keeps him on the field on passing downs.

4866.outlook: Looking to rebound in his ninth season after a clear step back in 2025 following a 378-touch workload the year before. Philadelphia's offensive structure still funnels goal-line work through Jalen Hurts, which caps his touchdown share. NBC is the outlier at RB6 while the other four sit at RB10-11. Market value has fallen, and the backfield behind him is thin with Elijah Mitchell on IR.
4866.watch: Age-and-mileage regression -- the 2024 workload is the kind that historically shows up a year or two later.

13287.outlook: The No. 3 overall pick, with good size and 4.36 speed and a three-down skill set, installed immediately as Arizona's lead back. James Conner (foot) is behind him and Tyler Allgeier is a complement. This is the widest source disagreement in the top 15 at the position -- ESPN has him RB7, CBS RB15 -- which is the honest read on a rookie with no NFL usage to price. Rostered in every league.
13287.watch: Whether Arizona trusts him on passing downs from Week 1, which is what separates RB7 from RB15.

8130.outlook: Trails only Ja'Marr Chase in targets (317) and receptions (252) over the past two seasons, which makes him a receiver in a tight end's body. Arizona's quarterback situation is unsettled between Jacoby Brissett and rookie Carson Beck, but McBride's target share has held up regardless of who has played. Healthy. Four of five sources have him TE1 or TE2.
8130.watch: The quarterback decision -- a rookie start would likely mean more checkdowns to him, not fewer.

3198.outlook: Finished second in the NFL in rushing yards for the fourth time in 2025 and is still the early-down and goal-line back at 32. His market value has risen more than almost any back in the past 30 days, which is unusual for a player at this age and suggests drafters are betting on one more full season. Justice Hill handles passing downs, which caps his PPR ceiling. Sources spread him RB8 to RB13.
3198.watch: The first sign of a genuine workload split -- at 32 it would arrive without warning.

8151.outlook: Moved to Kansas City and is listed as the clear lead back with Emmett Johnson and Emari Demercado behind him. The upside is obvious if Patrick Mahomes is healthy; the risk is that Mahomes is listed questionable with a knee (ACL) designation and Justin Fields is the backup, which would reshape the offense. Market value is rising. Sources spread him RB10 to RB15.
8151.watch: Mahomes' knee -- it is the dominant variable for every Kansas City skill player.

8112.outlook: Aiming for a third straight top-15 finish in receiver fantasy points per game. He is the clear alpha in Atlanta with Kyle Pitts as the secondary threat and Bijan Robinson absorbing the ground work. Sources agree tightly at WR5-7. Healthy, with market value drifting up.
8112.watch: Tua Tagovailoa's back -- London's efficiency depends on accurate, on-time throws.

4984.outlook: Has finished no worse than second among quarterbacks in fantasy points in each of the past six seasons, and all five sources have him QB1 unanimously. His rushing floor is the reason: passing volume has been down the past two years without denting his fantasy output. DJ Moore is a genuine upgrade to the receiver room. Healthy at 30, and his market value is climbing.
4984.watch: Nothing structural -- the only realistic risk is missed time.

9224.outlook: Cincinnati's lead back for a third season, and the receiving role is what makes him a top-10 PPR option in a pass-heavy offense with almost no depth behind Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. This is the biggest source disagreement among top-15 backs: CBS has him RB5 and FantasyPros RB6, while ESPN has him RB12. Market value is rising sharply. Samaje Perine is the only competition.
9224.watch: Whether the 2025 slow start (10.1 points per game early) was a fluke or a usage pattern.

11604.outlook: A late-game injury in Week 1 last year cost him three weeks and dulled a season that started with 103 yards. He remains the focal point of the Las Vegas passing game with a thin receiver room around him. The offense is the concern: rookie Fernando Mendoza is listed ahead of Kirk Cousins. Market value has fallen meaningfully over the past month, the largest drop among top-two tight ends.
11604.watch: Whether a rookie quarterback leans on him as a safety valve or simply produces fewer total plays.

11632.outlook: On the comeback trail from a torn ACL that limited him to four games last season, and he is still carrying a questionable designation in August. When healthy he has commanded a 35% target share across 18 full career games, which is elite. The receiver room behind him is thin and banged up, so the volume is there if the knee is. FantasyPros shows the widest rank deviation of any top-15 receiver on him.
11632.watch: Practice participation -- a full-go report changes his price immediately.

8137.outlook: Drew the franchise tag from Dallas after a career year in which he ranked near the top of the position in catches, yards, touchdowns and end-zone targets. His market value is up sharply. The friction is contractual, not on-field: his 2026 season is widely framed as his last in Dallas, and CeeDee Lamb is publicly lobbying for him to be paid. Sources are tightly grouped at WR10-13.
8137.watch: Whether Dallas's target split between him and Lamb holds at last year's rate.

8155.outlook: Returns on the franchise tag as the Jets' lead back with Braelon Allen behind him. He has struggled to convert talent into fantasy production inside two underwhelming offenses, and Geno Smith at quarterback is a modest rather than transformative upgrade. Market value has fallen. Sources are grouped at RB13-17 with no strong dissent.
8155.watch: Whether the receiving usage returns -- his PPR case rests on it, not on carries.

7569.outlook: Has cleared 1,000 yards when on the field but has never played a full 17-game season, which is the entire debate on him. He is the unambiguous No. 1 in Houston, and Tank Dell's slow return from a major knee injury concentrates targets further. C.J. Stroud is healthy. Four of five sources have him WR8-9.
7569.watch: Availability -- the per-game production has never been the question.

5859.outlook: Traded to New England in June and now catches passes from Drake Maye, who is sitting out the preseason opener as a precaution. Brown has finished top-15 in receiver points per game in each of his recent seasons and the room behind him is thin, so target share should be high. Market value has softened slightly on the change of scenery. FantasyPros is highest at WR8.
5859.watch: How quickly the timing with Maye develops -- a slow start would be scheme, not decline.

8150.outlook: Has produced 1,350-plus scrimmage yards in three straight seasons including a career-high 1,533 in 2025, yet the market never fully trusts him because Blake Corum is always lurking. Nothing has changed on that front this camp. Healthy, in a good offense with Matthew Stafford. Market value has fallen modestly. Sources are grouped at RB13-17.
8150.watch: Any real change in the Corum split -- three years of evidence says it will not come.

5850.outlook: His 2025 splits cleanly into a strong pre-injury stretch and a diminished post-injury one, and he is currently listed questionable with a groin issue at 28. He remains Green Bay's clear lead back with MarShawn Lloyd behind him. Market value is rising. Sources spread him RB12 to RB17.
5850.watch: The groin -- soft-tissue issues at his age and workload tend to recur.

8144.outlook: Coming off a career year with highs in targets (156), receptions (100), yards (1,163) and touchdowns (nine), finishing eighth among receivers in points per game. Tyler Shough enters Year 2 as the starter and is a common breakout pick. Olave's market value has risen more than almost any receiver in the past month. Rookie Jordyn Tyson is the only real target competition.
8144.watch: Shough's development -- Olave's ceiling now moves with his quarterback's.

7588.outlook: Re-signed with Dallas after finishing 12th among backs following three unproductive seasons in Denver. He is the lead back with Jaydon Blue as the change of pace. Sources agree tightly at RB16-18, an unusually clean consensus. The offense should score plenty with Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens.
7588.watch: Jaydon Blue's role -- if Blue takes passing downs, Williams becomes a two-down back in a PPR league.

7525.outlook: Enters his sixth season as Philadelphia's top receiver and is currently limited with a hamstring issue. His market value has risen sharply, one of the biggest moves among receivers in the past 30 days. Sources disagree moderately: CBS and FantasyPros have him WR13 while NBC has him WR19. The offense's run-heavy identity is the ceiling constraint, not his role.
7525.watch: The hamstring -- and whether Philadelphia throws more than its 2025 rate.

8146.outlook: Bouncing back from an injury-shortened 2025 that limited him to seven games, the first time he had missed any. He is the clear No. 1 in New York with Geno Smith now throwing to him, a real upgrade over recent seasons. This is the widest disagreement among top-20 receivers: ESPN has him WR10, CBS and NBC WR20. Market value is flat.
8146.watch: Whether Smith's arrival lifts the offense enough to justify ESPN's price rather than the consensus one.

12481.outlook: Year 2 breakout candidate after an impressive but injury-shortened rookie season in which he averaged 16.0 fantasy points per game once he took the job in Week 2. He is the lead back with Tyrone Tracy Jr. behind him. Market value is up sharply. The offense should improve if Jaxson Dart takes the expected Year 2 step.
12481.watch: Durability -- the rookie season ended early and his running style is high-contact.

12526.outlook: The reigning Offensive Rookie of the Year and a candidate to enter the elite tier after a strong debut as the eighth overall pick in 2025. He is the clear alpha in Carolina with no real target competition. The quarterback is the question: Bryce Young enters Year 4 still unproven. NBC is highest at WR12, CBS lowest at WR21.
12526.watch: Bryce Young's efficiency -- McMillan's target volume is safe, his scoring is not.

12529.outlook: Enters Year 2 after a roller-coaster rookie season with three enormous games (28-plus points) but otherwise a secondary role behind Rhamondre Stevenson. His market value has fallen more sharply than any other back in the top 25, which says drafters no longer expect a clean takeover. Sources agree tightly at RB22-25. A.J. Brown's arrival should improve the offense around him.
12529.watch: Whether the Stevenson split resolves -- the boom games prove the talent, not the volume.

12514.outlook: A genuinely difficult evaluation: five touchdowns and 20.5 fantasy points per game through his first five rookie games, then a collapse from there. He is Tampa Bay's leading receiver with Chris Godwin and Jalen McMillan (calf) behind him. Sources are grouped at WR16-20. Market value is flat.
12514.watch: Which version of his rookie season is the real one -- there is no middle case priced in.

4881.outlook: Not in line to play in the preseason opener, which is routine. He is the consensus QB2 behind Josh Allen with the same rushing-floor argument, and he has been working closely with rookie receiver Lane. Zay Flowers (quadriceps) is his top target. Market value is rising.
4881.watch: Baltimore's receiver health -- Jackson's passing volume depends on it more than his rushing does.

7543.outlook: Signed with New Orleans to lead the backfield with Alvin Kamara now in a complementary role. His market value has collapsed over the past 30 days, the sharpest drop of any back in the top 25, which suggests drafters expect a committee rather than a takeover. Expert ranks have not moved with it, so this is a genuine market-versus-expert split. Tyler Shough is the quarterback.
7543.watch: Whether Kamara's snap share stays meaningful -- the market is betting it does.

12512.outlook: Entering Year 2 after a rookie season bookended by an off-field absence and a strong 14-game stretch in between. He is the lead back with Dylan Sampson behind him. Market value has fallen. The offense is the problem: Shedeur Sanders and Deshaun Watson are still splitting the starter designation, and Cleveland's scoring environment is poor.
12512.watch: The quarterback resolution -- Judkins' touchdown equity depends on Cleveland reaching the red zone.

10229.outlook: Enters Year 4 still without a full season as a starter, having missed most of 2024 to injury and nine more games since. When on the field he has been highly efficient in Kansas City's offense. Market value is rising and sources disagree sharply: Fantasy Football Calculator has him WR6, NBC WR14. Xavier Worthy (shoulder) is the other primary target.
10229.watch: Patrick Mahomes' knee designation -- everything about Rice's price assumes Mahomes plays.

6801.outlook: Overshadowed by Ja'Marr Chase but has remained a key red-zone piece in a pass-friendly offense, producing despite missing seven games last season. Cincinnati's skill group is unusually healthy this camp. Sources spread him WR13 to WR22, one of the wider gaps in the top 20, reflecting disagreement about whether the second receiver in this offense is a WR2 or a WR1.
6801.watch: Health -- he has not played a full season recently, and the per-game production has never been the issue.

12518.outlook: A solid rookie season that was better than the surface numbers: five touchdowns and 13.1 fantasy points per game across 12 games with a healthy Daniel Jones. All five sources have him exactly TE4. Market value is rising. The Indianapolis quarterback competition between Jones and Anthony Richardson is unresolved and directly affects him.
12518.watch: The quarterback decision -- his rookie splits show a clear gap between Jones and the alternative.

11584.outlook: Coming off a disappointing 2025 in which he missed seven games and lost efficiency after a 5.42 yards-per-carry rookie season. He remains the lead back with Kenny Gainwell complementing him. Sources agree tightly at RB19-22. Market value is flat, and Tampa Bay's line is dealing with a Tristan Wirfs hamstring issue.
11584.watch: Whether the efficiency returns -- the volume is not in doubt, the yards-per-touch is.

7526.outlook: Traded to Denver after five seasons in Miami, where he was a consistent top-30 fantasy receiver. He now shares a room with Courtland Sutton in a Bo Nix offense, and he is carrying an undisclosed injury early in camp along with several other Denver receivers. Market value is rising. Sources spread him WR19 to WR25.
7526.watch: Whether he or Sutton emerges as the primary target -- Denver has not made that clear.

6770.outlook: Bouncing back from an injury-shortened 2025 (eight games) and he has now missed at least six games in three of six pro seasons, which is the whole risk case. He is set to play in the preseason opener, a good sign. The supporting cast is elite and Cincinnati's skill group is unusually healthy. Four of five sources have him QB4.
6770.watch: Durability -- his per-game production has never been in question.

9997.outlook: Posted career bests in target share (29%), targets, catches and yards in 2025 and is Baltimore's clear No. 1. He is currently listed questionable with a quadriceps issue. Market value is rising. Lamar Jackson's rushing-heavy offense caps total passing volume, which is why he sits WR13-17 rather than higher.
9997.watch: The quadriceps -- and whether Baltimore's rookie receivers cut into his target share.

11564.outlook: Coming off a breakout second season and now throws to A.J. Brown, acquired in June. He is sitting out the preseason opener, which is precautionary rather than an injury. Consensus QB3 with Fantasy Football Calculator highest at QB2. His market value is flat despite the receiver upgrade.
11564.watch: How quickly the Brown connection develops -- the rest of the receiver room is thin.

11635.outlook: Rebound candidate after falling short of expectations in 2025, following a rookie year with an 82-1,155-7 line and a 12th-place finish among receivers. He is the primary target in a Justin Herbert offense that is described as still settling into a new scheme. Healthy, and market value is rising. Sources agree tightly at WR17-23.
11635.watch: How the new offensive scheme distributes targets -- his rookie usage was slot-heavy.

5892.outlook: Traded to Houston after seven seasons in Chicago and Detroit, coming off a down 2025 with career lows. He is the lead back with Woody Marks as the change of pace, in an offense that should be competent with C.J. Stroud. This is a touchdown-dependent profile in full PPR. Fantasy Football Calculator is the low outlier at RB30.
5892.watch: Woody Marks' passing-down share -- it directly caps Montgomery's PPR floor.

13286.outlook: Drafted 32nd overall by Seattle and walks into an unusually open situation: Zach Charbonnet opened camp on PUP with a torn ACL. Price himself is listed questionable with a lower-body issue. He managed only 280 career carries at Notre Dame behind Jeremiyah Love, so the college workload is thin. Market value has risen sharply and all five sources cluster him at RB26-28.
13286.watch: His own health -- the job is available if he is.

12517.outlook: The single clearest usage trend on the board: 4.1 targets and 8.5 fantasy points per game across his first 14 NFL games, then 12.0 targets (10-plus in each) and 20.0 points per game over his final four. All five sources have him exactly TE3. Healthy, and market value is rising. Caleb Williams enters Year 3 with Luther Burden III (groin) limited.
12517.watch: Whether the late-season target volume holds once Burden is healthy.

6790.outlook: Entering his seventh season and third in Chicago, having cleared 1,300 scrimmage yards in each of the past two years. Rookie Kyle Monangai is the push behind him. The receiving work is what keeps him a usable PPR back rather than a touchdown-dependent one. Sources agree tightly at RB20-24.
6790.watch: Monangai's early-down share -- Swift's PPR value survives it, his rushing volume does not.

2133.outlook: At 33 he is the complementary piece to Puka Nacua rather than the alpha, but Matthew Stafford has historically supported two productive receivers. Market value is rising. Sources spread him WR19 to WR25. Healthy with no designation.
2133.watch: Age-related decline -- there is no injury or role concern, only the calendar.

11566.outlook: Bouncing back from a 2025 that limited him to seven games, after an Offensive Rookie of the Year debut. His rushing floor is why ESPN has him QB2 while Fantasy Football Calculator has him QB7. His market value has fallen meaningfully. Left tackle Laremy Tunsil's torn triceps is a real hit to his protection.
11566.watch: The Tunsil replacement -- a compromised line raises both his rushing volume and his injury risk.

11560.outlook: Enters Year 3 after finishing no lower than 11th among quarterbacks in 2025. The expert market has cooled: he fell from QB7 to QB12 in this blend, and his market value is down. FantasyPros is the clear outlier at QB7 while Fantasy Football Calculator has him QB15. Colston Loveland's late-season emergence is a genuine positive.
11560.watch: Whether the 2025 leap was the new baseline or the ceiling.

13279.outlook: Drafted fourth overall by Tennessee and immediately the top receiver on the depth chart. He was efficient rather than high-volume at Ohio State (13.1 yards per reception). This is one of the widest disagreements on the board: ESPN has him WR25, Fantasy Football Calculator WR38, with the largest FantasyPros standard deviation of any receiver in this range. Cam Ward enters Year 2.
13279.watch: Whether Tennessee throws enough to support a rookie alpha -- the offense projects low-volume.

4983.outlook: Traded to Buffalo, which is a major environment upgrade: Josh Allen's offense is the best scoring situation available to a receiver. His market value has risen sharply. Sources spread him WR23 to WR29. Khalil Shakir and Keon Coleman are the competition for targets.
4983.watch: Whether Buffalo funnels enough volume to a single receiver -- historically it has not.

4046.outlook: Listed questionable with a knee (ACL) designation entering his 10th season, which is the dominant fact about him and about every Kansas City skill player. He followed two disappointing fantasy seasons with an elite 2025 start. His market value has fallen sharply. NBC is far higher on him at QB9 than the other four sources.
4046.watch: The knee -- his ADP and rank both assume he opens the season.

8228.outlook: Career highs in touches (251), yards (1,291) and touchdowns (eight) last season, good for 13.6 fantasy points per game. Pittsburgh then signed Rico Dowdle, and the two are ranked one spot apart, which is the honest read on a true committee. His market value has risen sharply anyway. Aaron Rodgers is the quarterback.
8228.watch: The Dowdle split -- neither back is priced as a workhorse and neither has separated.

11620.outlook: Opened 2025 with five touchdowns in four games and 15-plus fantasy points in each, then faded badly. He shares a room with Luther Burden III (groin) and Colston Loveland, who has emerged as a genuine target competitor. Market value is flat. Sources are grouped at WR24-30.
11620.watch: Whether Loveland's late-season target surge comes out of Odunze's share.

6797.outlook: Ranked just inside the top 10 in attempts, yards and touchdowns last season and added real rushing value. He is described as getting comfortable in a new offense, which is the reason for the spread: NBC, CBS and FantasyPros have him QB8, ESPN QB14. Market value is flat. Ladd McConkey and Omarion Hampton are the weapons.
6797.watch: How the new scheme uses his legs -- the rushing points are what separate QB8 from QB14.

12490.outlook: Positioned to take over lead-back duties after Travis Etienne Jr. left, having played sparingly as a rookie (83 carries, 14 targets in 15 games). His market value is up sharply and all five sources agree tightly at RB23-25. The complication is that he is only rostered in about two-thirds of leagues, so the market is still catching up.
12490.watch: Chris Rodriguez's role -- a genuine committee would undo the entire thesis.

5927.outlook: Bounce-back candidate after a lost 2025 in which he missed seven games and Jayden Daniels missed 10. He is the clear No. 1 in Washington at 30. His market value has fallen more than most receivers in this range, likely age plus the Stefon Diggs addition. Sources are grouped tightly at WR21-25.
5927.watch: Daniels' health -- the two players' fantasy seasons are effectively the same bet.

12519.outlook: Sidelined with a groin injury in early August, which is the immediate issue. He is the second receiver in Chicago behind Rome Odunze, with Colston Loveland taking a growing share. His market value is rising despite the injury, and he is rostered in only about 78% of leagues, so there is still acquisition room. Sources are grouped at WR22-27.
12519.watch: The groin timeline -- missing camp reps in a crowded room is how young receivers lose roles.

2216.outlook: Signed with San Francisco after 12 seasons in Tampa Bay and is listed questionable with a quadriceps issue at 33, though he did practice this week. This is the widest source disagreement among top-30 receivers: NBC has him WR21, ESPN WR35. Market value is falling. Brock Purdy and a thin room around him support the volume case.
2216.watch: The quadriceps and the calendar -- at 33, a soft-tissue issue in August is not routine.

9484.outlook: Was on the cusp of a breakout before a torn ACL in Week 9 last season, and he is still listed questionable with that knee. The rest of Green Bay's tight end room is decimated -- Luke Musgrave, Luke Lachey and RJ Maryland are all out -- so the role is his if healthy. Sources have him TE6-11, and his market value is falling.
9484.watch: Whether the knee is genuinely ready -- the depth chart is clear, the health is not.

13281.outlook: Drafted eighth overall by New Orleans and led the rookie class with a 35% college target share. He is the second receiver behind Chris Olave in a Tyler Shough offense. Market value is rising. Sources spread him WR32 to WR40, a normal rookie gap.
13281.watch: Whether Shough's Year 2 leap arrives -- Tyson's ceiling is capped by the offense, not the depth chart.

11631.outlook: Jacksonville's nominal No. 1 but in a genuinely crowded room with Parker Washington, Jakobi Meyers and Travis Hunter, which is why no Jaguars receiver is priced as an alpha. Sources spread him WR29 to WR40. Market value is flat. Trevor Lawrence is coming off a strong season.
11631.watch: Whether Jacksonville concentrates targets -- four viable receivers is the problem, not his talent.

6904.outlook: Tossed a career-high 25 touchdowns last season but his rushing production fell off sharply (105-421-8), which is where his fantasy edge has always come from. Sources agree tightly at QB5-8. Market value is flat. Saquon Barkley's presence keeps competing for goal-line work.
6904.watch: Whether the rushing touchdowns return -- that line item alone is the difference between QB5 and QB12.

11628.outlook: All five sources have him within one spot at WR31-33, unusually tight agreement for a player whose market value has collapsed over the past 30 days -- one of the largest drops on the board. That gap between stable expert ranks and falling market price is the interesting thing about him. Arizona's quarterback situation is unresolved between Jacoby Brissett and Carson Beck. Healthy.
11628.watch: The quarterback decision -- the market appears to be pricing in a downgrade the experts have not.

8148.outlook: Has delivered 1,000-plus-yard seasons in each of the past two years and is now firmly established as Detroit's second receiver. Market value is rising. Sources agree tightly at WR22-28. Amon-Ra St. Brown and Sam LaPorta are ahead of him in the target hierarchy.
8148.watch: Whether Detroit's tight end emphasis, which Jared Goff has spoken about, comes out of his share.

12524.outlook: Listed as Cleveland's starter but Deshaun Watson is reportedly being carried as a co-starter, so the job is not settled. He made eight appearances as a rookie without much production. Four sources have him tightly at QB32-33. Superflex leagues are the only realistic place he matters.
12524.watch: The depth chart resolution -- and whether Cleveland's offense can support any fantasy quarterback.

4217.outlook: On the PUP list with an Achilles injury and listed OUT by ESPN, which the consensus TE10 ranking does not reflect. He has played one full season in his career (2018) and the injury pattern is the entire profile. When available he is a top-five tight end. Market value is flat, which suggests the market has not fully priced the PUP designation.
4217.watch: The PUP designation -- a player who cannot open the season should not be drafted as TE10.

7594.outlook: Coming off a disappointing 2025 in which he battled injury and lost lead-back duties to Rico Dowdle, finishing with 734 yards on 164 touches. He opens as Carolina's lead back with Jonathon Brooks ranked just behind him and neither separating. Market value is flat and he is rostered in only about 80% of leagues. Sources are grouped at RB29-34.
7594.watch: Jonathon Brooks' health -- if Brooks is right, this becomes a split rather than a job.

7021.outlook: Signed with Pittsburgh after nearly identical seasons in Dallas (1,328 yards, five touchdowns) and Carolina (1,373 yards, seven touchdowns). He is in a true committee with Jaylen Warren, ranked one spot apart. His market value is rising. Aaron Rodgers gives the offense a reasonable scoring floor.
7021.watch: Which back takes passing downs -- that is the whole difference in a PPR league.

11565.outlook: Lost the Minnesota starting job to Kyler Murray, the most consequential camp decision of the week. He missed his entire rookie season and struggled through 10 games in 2025. Only three sources rank him at all, all around QB36. He is a superflex stash, not a starter.
11565.watch: A Murray injury -- that is the only path back to relevance this season.

6768.outlook: Signed with Atlanta and is the starter but is listed questionable with a back issue, with Michael Penix Jr. (knee, ACL) behind him. Four sources have him QB27-32. His fantasy relevance is marginal outside superflex, but his health matters enormously for Drake London, Bijan Robinson and Kyle Pitts.
6768.watch: The back -- and whether Penix is healthy enough to be a real alternative.

10859.outlook: Has settled in as a top-10 tight end but has never matched his rookie production. The new information is that Jared Goff has publicly said Detroit needs to find more ways to get him the ball, which is the kind of camp signal that sometimes precedes a target bump. Healthy, market value rising, and sources agree tightly at TE5-8.
10859.watch: Whether the stated intent converts into actual targets -- Amon-Ra St. Brown is still the priority.

12489.outlook: Looking to overtake J.K. Dobbins as Denver's lead back; in the 10 games both were active last season, Harvey handled 50 carries to Dobbins' 153. He is listed as RB2 on the depth chart. Market value is rising and FantasyPros and Fantasy Football Calculator have him a full five spots higher than CBS. Dobbins is carrying an undisclosed injury.
12489.watch: Whether the snap split actually flips -- last year's split says it has not yet.

7553.outlook: Ranked TE5-8 by all five sources, the highest consensus of his career, in a role where he is Atlanta's secondary passing option behind Drake London. Healthy with no designation and a flat market. Tua Tagovailoa's back is the offense-level risk.
7553.watch: Red-zone usage -- his ranking assumes touchdown regression in his favour, which has not arrived before.

8167.outlook: A boom-bust career on full display in 2025: missed the first seven games, then produced multiple big fantasy weeks on return. He is nominally Green Bay's top receiver in a genuine committee with Jayden Reed and Matthew Golden. Sources spread him WR26 to WR37, one of the widest gaps in this range. Market value is flat.
8167.watch: Whether Green Bay ever concentrates targets -- three years of evidence says no.

5967.outlook: Has handled 67.2% of Tennessee's designed rushing attempts since arriving (15.2 per game) and still finished only 22nd and 30th in fantasy, which is the argument against him: volume without efficiency or receiving work. Tyjae Spears splits in. Market value is falling. Sources agree tightly at RB26-30.
5967.watch: Whether Tennessee's offense improves enough to make his volume worth anything.

11559.outlook: Listed as Atlanta's QB2 behind Tua Tagovailoa and working back from ACL surgery. His market value has collapsed over the past 30 days, one of the largest drops among quarterbacks. Only three sources rank him, around QB33-35. He is a superflex stash contingent on Tagovailoa's back issue.
11559.watch: Tagovailoa's back -- Penix's entire 2026 value is a backup-quarterback bet.

1373.outlook: Traded to the Jets, where he began his career, and is in line to start. Four sources have him tightly at QB28-30. At 35 he is a floor-not-ceiling option, relevant mainly in superflex. His arrival is a modest upgrade for Garrett Wilson and Breece Hall.
1373.watch: Nothing on his own profile -- his value is as a stabiliser for the Jets skill players.

3257.outlook: Back for a second season in Arizona and positioned as the probable Week 1 starter after a surprising 2025. Rookie Carson Beck is pushing him and the staff has been publicly complimentary of Beck. Four sources have him QB23-30. CBS is notably higher at QB23.
3257.watch: The Beck decision -- Trey McBride's target volume has held up under either quarterback, but the offense's efficiency would not.

6806.outlook: Re-signed with Denver and is listed as the depth chart RB1, but he is carrying an undisclosed injury and RJ Harvey is closing. Last season with both active, Dobbins out-carried Harvey 153 to 50. Market value is rising and he is rostered in only about 69% of leagues. Sources agree tightly at RB33-36.
6806.watch: His health -- Denver's committee resolves in Harvey's favour the moment Dobbins misses time.

11586.outlook: Has spent two seasons as Kyren Williams' backup and that is the expectation again. NBC is a striking outlier at RB28 while the other four have him RB35-42. His market value is rising, which usually signals handcuff demand rather than a role change. Williams is healthy.
11586.watch: A Kyren Williams injury -- Corum is one of the cleanest one-for-one handcuffs on the board.

7567.outlook: Signed with Tampa Bay after a second-half breakout in Pittsburgh where he averaged 13.3 touches, 85.0 yards and 17.8 fantasy points. He is the complementary back to Bucky Irving. Market value is rising sharply. ESPN is highest at RB31, NBC lowest at RB39.
7567.watch: Whether he takes passing downs from Irving -- that is what would make him startable in PPR.

7523.outlook: Coming off a breakout 2025 in which he ranked no lower than seventh among quarterbacks in attempts, completions, yards and touchdowns. Four sources have him QB8-10 with NBC the outlier at QB15. Market value is flat. The receiver room is deep but unconcentrated, which supports passing volume.
7523.watch: Whether the 2025 breakout holds -- it was his first genuinely good fantasy season.

5045.outlook: Has produced 1,000 yards and a top-20 fantasy finish in each of the past two seasons. Jaylen Waddle's arrival is the complication, and sources disagree sharply as a result: ESPN has him WR29, NBC WR43. His market value is rising, which suggests drafters are siding with the optimistic read. Healthy.
5045.watch: Whether Denver's target hierarchy actually changes -- Sutton has been the priority for two straight years.

7611.outlook: Will battle TreVeyon Henderson for New England touches; last season Stevenson usually held the larger share. His market value is falling. All five sources are grouped tightly at RB28-33. A.J. Brown's arrival should raise the offense's efficiency.
7611.watch: Whether Henderson finally takes the job -- the market is betting on it slowly.

1466.outlook: Re-signed with Kansas City for what may be his final season, and his days as an elite producer are behind him. All five sources have him TE9-11, which is an honest read. Market value is falling. Patrick Mahomes' knee designation is an additional risk.
1466.watch: Mahomes' availability -- Kelce's remaining value is entirely volume-based.

13311.outlook: Third-round rookie on PUP with a torn ACL and listed OUT, so he will not contribute early. At 222 pounds he is the heaviest receiver in his class and profiles as a perimeter possession target. He is fourth on Miami's depth chart. Ranked around WR81-95 by three sources.
13311.watch: Return timeline -- he is a late-season stash at best.

1166.outlook: Signed with Las Vegas and lost the starting job to rookie Fernando Mendoza on the depth chart, and he was held out of practice after an altercation involving Maxx Crosby. At 38 he is a superflex-only option. Three sources have him around QB34-35.
1166.watch: The Mendoza decision -- and whether the situation in Las Vegas stays workable.

4017.outlook: Expected back on the field after four lost years in Cleveland and is reportedly being listed as a co-starter with Shedeur Sanders. He was a top-six fantasy quarterback by points per game in each of his first four seasons, which is now ancient history. Three sources have him around QB31-35.
4017.watch: Whether he actually wins the job -- and whether that matters for Cleveland's skill players.

3294.outlook: Coming off a season in which he led the NFL in completions and ranked no lower than fourth in dropbacks, attempts and yards. He throws to CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, one of the best receiver duos in the league. Market value is falling slightly. Sources spread him QB5 to QB10.
3294.watch: Health -- his fantasy profile is volume-based and he has missed extended time before.

11637.outlook: Has struggled to make an impact since going 33rd overall in 2024 and is now third on Buffalo's depth chart behind DJ Moore and Khalil Shakir. Sources disagree widely, from WR85 to WR119. Market value is up slightly. This is a talent-versus-role bet with the role currently losing.
11637.watch: A Buffalo receiver injury -- he needs vacated targets, not development.

4199.outlook: At 31 he splits Minnesota's backfield with Jordan Mason and neither has separated. Kyler Murray's arrival as starter adds rushing competition near the goal line. Sources spread him RB33 to RB42. Market value is falling.
4199.watch: The Mason split -- neither back is priced as a starter and the committee looks real.

13294.outlook: Drafted 20th overall by Philadelphia and posted the best yards-per-route-run mark in his rookie class despite modest size. He is listed as the second slot receiver behind DeVonta Smith and is currently questionable. Sources spread him WR34 to WR52, a wide rookie range. Market value is falling.
13294.watch: Whether Philadelphia's run-heavy offense supports a third receiver at all.

12497.outlook: Had the look of a Day 3 find in 2025 before a season-ending shin injury in Week 9. He is now fourth on Seattle's depth chart behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Rashid Shaheed and Cooper Kupp. Three sources have him around WR85-94. Healthy now.
12497.watch: A Kupp or Shaheed absence -- he needs a path to snaps before anything else.

9753.outlook: Would have entered 2026 as Seattle's clear lead back, but a torn ACL in the playoff loss to San Francisco has him on PUP and listed OUT. Rookie Jadarian Price is taking the reps. Sources still rank him RB42-49, which prices a return rather than a lost season. Market value is rising.
9753.watch: His activation date -- the Seattle job is genuinely open if he gets back in time.

13317.outlook: Undrafted-level profile as a rookie fourth on Tampa Bay's depth chart behind Emeka Egbuka, Chris Godwin and Jalen McMillan. Sources disagree widely (WR71 to WR99), which is normal for a player with no NFL usage. Market value is falling. He is a deep dynasty flier, not a redraft asset.
13317.watch: Injuries ahead of him -- there is no other route to snaps this season.

12533.outlook: One of the biggest August risers in published rankings, jumping nearly 30 spots in some sets, and his market value is up sharply. He played a 39% snap share as a seventh-round rookie and is now listed as Washington's depth chart RB1 ahead of Rachaad White. He is rostered in only about 74% of leagues. CBS is highest at RB32.
12533.watch: Whether Washington names him the clear starter -- the split with White is the only thing holding his price down.

5846.outlook: Year 2 in Pittsburgh and currently listed questionable with an unspecified injury, alongside fellow starter Michael Pittman Jr. (leg). Aaron Rodgers is the quarterback, which should stabilise the passing game. Sources are grouped at WR32-38 and his market value is flat.
5846.watch: The undisclosed injury -- an August designation with no named body part usually resolves quickly or not at all.

10232.outlook: Averaged 4.3 targets and 7.6 fantasy points per game earlier in his career and is now Arizona's clear No. 2 behind Marvin Harrison Jr., with Trey McBride absorbing a large target share. All five sources agree tightly at WR39-42 and his market value is rising.
10232.watch: The Arizona quarterback decision -- a rookie start would likely mean more short, high-volume targets for him.

9487.outlook: A strong finish to 2025 made him one of the more discussed sleepers of this offseason, and his market value is up sharply. The problem is the depth chart: Brian Thomas Jr., Jakobi Meyers and Travis Hunter are all competing for the same targets. He is rostered in only about 74% of leagues. CBS is highest at WR30.
9487.watch: Whether Jacksonville's target distribution ever concentrates -- four receivers cannot all hit.

9504.outlook: Was a cut or trade candidate for much of the 2025 offseason and is now third on New England's depth chart behind A.J. Brown. Sources spread him WR69 to WR86. Market value is up slightly. He is a bench flier in deeper leagues only.
9504.watch: An injury ahead of him -- the room behind Brown is thin enough that one absence changes his role.

6819.outlook: Traded to Pittsburgh and listed questionable with a leg issue. This is the widest source disagreement among top-40 receivers: ESPN has him WR30, NBC WR51. Aaron Rodgers is a reasonable quarterback upgrade over recent seasons, and DK Metcalf is also banged up.
6819.watch: Which of the two Pittsburgh receivers gets healthy first -- the target hierarchy is genuinely unset.

11563.outlook: Finished seventh among quarterbacks in his second season and now has Jaylen Waddle added to the receiver room. ESPN is the outlier at QB10 while NBC has him QB18. His market value is falling. Denver's defence being the consensus No. 1 unit means fewer trailing game scripts, which caps passing volume.
11563.watch: Whether the Waddle addition raises his passing volume or just redistributes it.

4035.outlook: Entering his age-31 season with real uncertainty after New Orleans brought in Travis Etienne Jr. to lead the backfield. He is listed as RB2 on the depth chart. Market value is rising and he is rostered in only about 77% of leagues. Sources spread him RB43 to RB55.
4035.watch: Whether he keeps the passing-down role -- it is the only thing that would make him startable in PPR.

10213.outlook: Nominally Las Vegas's No. 1 receiver, which says more about the room than about him. Brock Bowers dominates the target share and rookie Fernando Mendoza is the likely starter. All five sources cluster him at WR59-66 and his market value is falling.
10213.watch: Whether Las Vegas throws to receivers at all -- Bowers and Michael Mayer absorb a lot of it.

13296.outlook: Third-round rookie sitting third on Miami's receiver depth chart in an offense quarterbacked by Malik Willis. His market value has risen sharply but that is off a very low base. Sources disagree widely, from WR85 to WR108.
13296.watch: Whether Miami's passing game is functional at all -- no Dolphins receiver is startable if it is not.

13268.outlook: Fourth-round rookie who is fourth on Baltimore's depth chart behind Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman. Sources spread him from WR80 to WR124, the widest gap of any receiver in this range. Baltimore's run-heavy offense limits receiver volume generally.
13268.watch: A move up the depth chart -- there is nothing else to watch this season.

13274.outlook: Second-round rookie sitting third in Pittsburgh's slot behind DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr., both of whom are currently banged up. His market value has collapsed over the past month, one of the largest drops on the board. Sources spread him WR65 to WR83.
13274.watch: Whether the injuries ahead of him linger into September -- that is his only path to snaps.

12483.outlook: A candidate for a Year 2 leap after an underwhelming rookie season as a 2025 second-round pick. He is third on the Las Vegas depth chart behind Tre Tucker. Sources spread him WR79 to WR97 and his market value is falling.
12483.watch: Whether he passes Tre Tucker -- the Raiders' No. 1 receiver spot is not well defended.

2449.outlook: Signed with Washington in August after being released, and he is the biggest riser in this refresh: FantasyPros moved him up 23 spots in a week and his positional rank climbed from WR63 to WR51. His market value is rising sharply. At 32 he is the No. 2 behind Terry McLaurin with Jayden Daniels throwing. CBS is highest at WR44.
2449.watch: How quickly he learns the offense -- an August signing usually means a slow September.

8183.outlook: Rebounding after injuries disrupted his 2025. The receiver room was rebuilt around Mike Evans (quadriceps) and Deebo Samuel, and Christian McCaffrey's practice absences are a concern for the whole offense. Fantasy Football Calculator is the clear outlier at QB6 against a QB11-13 consensus elsewhere.
8183.watch: McCaffrey's availability -- Purdy's efficiency has always been tied to the run game.

8136.outlook: Signed with Washington and is now listed as the depth chart RB2 behind Jacory Croskey-Merritt, who has been climbing rankings all August. White's market value has collapsed, one of the steepest drops on the board, and he is rostered in only about 62% of leagues. Sources still have him RB34-40.
8136.watch: Whether Washington confirms Croskey-Merritt as the starter -- the market has already decided.

11643.outlook: Competing again with Ollie Gordon II for backup reps behind De'Von Achane. His market value is rising. Three sources have him around RB66-70. Miami's coaching staff has publicly floated 40-plus touch games for Achane, which caps the backup role.
11643.watch: An Achane injury -- given the projected workload, this is a handcuff worth holding in deep leagues.
